name: Lesson 10 · Telling the time: the clock, the days, um and am

cards.note: Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. dreißig is the one ten written with ß; the others end in -zig.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. vier + zig: vierzig.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. fünf + zig: fünfzig.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. The unit comes first, then und, then the ten: one-and-twenty. eins loses its s.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. five-and-twenty, written as one word.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. fünf und vierzig, in one word. Say the unit first.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. zwei und dreißig: zweiunddreißig.
Numbers 21–59: the unit, und, the ten. acht und fünfzig. Read long numbers from the back: first the 8, then the 50.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. The hour, then Uhr: drei Uhr.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. German counts the half towards the next hour: halb vier is half to four, 3:30.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. 11:30 is halb zwölf: halfway to twelve.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. nach: past. Viertel nach zwei is 2:15.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. vor: to. Viertel vor zwölf is 11:45.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. Minutes, nach, then the hour; Uhr is left out.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. fünf vor neun: 8:55.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. German asks how late it is: Wie spät ist es?

cards.front: What time is it? – It's **twenty past four**.
cards.back: Wie viel Uhr ist es? – Es ist **zwanzig nach vier**.
cards.note: The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. Wie viel Uhr ist es? is the other way to ask. zwanzig nach vier: 4:20.
The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. Timetables use the 24-hour clock: the hour, Uhr, then the minutes.

cards.back: Der Zug fährt um **acht Uhr dreißig**.
cards.note: The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. The official way: acht Uhr dreißig. In speech, halb neun.

cards.back: Es ist **spät**, und ich bin müde.
cards.note: The clock: Uhr, halb, Viertel, vor, nach. spät: late. Es ist spät, with es as the subject, as in English.
um for clock times, am for days. um before a clock time: at.

cards.front: The train leaves **at** half past six.
cards.note: um for clock times, am for days. um halb sieben: at 6:30.
um for clock times, am for days. um sieben Uhr: at seven o'clock.

cards.front: **At what time** are you coming? (one friend)
cards.note: um for clock times, am for days. Um wie viel Uhr…? asks at what time; the whole phrase comes first, then the verb.
um for clock times, am for days. am before a day: am Montag. The days are all der-words.
um for clock times, am for days. am Dienstag first, so the verb comes second and wir after it.
um for clock times, am for days. am Mittwoch: Mittwoch means mid-week.
um for clock times, am for days. am Donnerstag, then ist second.
um for clock times, am for days. am Freitag: on Friday.
um for clock times, am for days. am Samstag, then the verb, then ich.
um for clock times, am for days. The subject meine Eltern comes after the verb.

cards.front: **On Sunday at three** my grandma is coming.
cards.back: **Am Sonntag um drei** kommt meine Oma.
cards.note: um for clock times, am for days. The day first, then the time: am Sonntag um drei. Together they take the first place.
um for clock times, am for days. After ist, a day takes no article and no am.
um for clock times, am for days. am Sonntag goes after the subject in a question.
um for clock times, am for days. am Samstag: on Saturday.
um for clock times, am for days. nicht comes after am Sonntag, like after heute.
